sections.title: What this module covers
sections.body: Sidekiq is the dominant background job framework in the Ruby ecosystem, and it appears in almost every intermediate-to-senior Rails interview. The architecture question is foundational: Sidekiq uses Redis as a queue (LPUSH to enqueue, BRPOP to dequeue), runs N threads per process, and processes jobs asynchronously. The idempotency question is the depth marker — Sidekiq retries failed jobs with exponential backoff, which means perform can be called multiple times for the same job. Your perform method must be safe to call multiple times with the same arguments. This page covers the full Sidekiq picture: architecture, queue priority, retry policy, the dead set, Sidekiq middleware, monitoring with Sidekiq Web, sidekiq-cron for scheduled jobs, and the comparison with Resque, GoodJob, and Delayed::Job.

sections.title: Key topics and depth markers
sections.body: Topics: sidekiq-architecture, job-patterns, retries-and-idempotency, middleware-monitoring. Each topic has dedicated Q&A covering the concept, the comparison, the internal mechanics, and the scenario-based questions interviewers use to test production understanding.

sections.title: How interviewers probe this module
sections.body: Interviewers at Rails-focused companies probe these topics by opening with a definition question, then immediately following up with when would you use X vs Y? and what are the gotchas?. The depth marker is always the trade-off and the failure mode — not just the API surface.
